column1: # A core's files (xpute-core io/file, the imports in ARCHITECTURE.md): what a core
# owes the runtime's completions of its opens. The runtime's own end — paths, reads, writes — is
# fs/file.tsv's; this is the core's, held across every core. A descriptor is a handle, so the
# trace binds them by name and holds them to relations, as handle.tsv does.
# The runtime completes an open, FS_OPEN tagged with its descriptor (spec/abi/fs.json), on a later
# turn however much later, with ECANCELED where its close came first; here a step completes it, so
# the completion can be made to arrive after the descriptor it names has closed.
# A failed open leaves no descriptor: the core's library lets its handle go as the completion is
# applied, so the core's own CLOSE of it finds nothing.
# An open is a descriptor of its own.
# The first is closed before its open was completed, and the next open takes its slot.
# The closed one's completion, ECANCELED, reaches no one — not its owner, 5, and not the slot's new
# one; the new one's reaches its owner, 6, alone; and the closed descriptor is not one to close again.
